fields.disciples: Nandarāma, also called Haripriyā (#482), author of the Kṛṣṇa-miśra-caritra
fields.notes: Disciple and attendant of Sītā-devī, Advaita's wife (Prema-vilāsa 24); did sādhana at Jaṅgalī-ṭoṭā (Maldah), where the Bādśāh of Gauḍa, who saw her now as a woman, now as a man, begged pardon and built her a house. The Sītā-caritra of Lokanātha dāsa says Jaṅgalī was a man, Yajñeśvara Cakravartī («Rājakumāra») of Hariharapura near Śāntipura. Vijayā-sakhī in Kṛṣṇa-līlā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 89).

An unnamed Vaiṣṇava of Vṛndāvana who came to see Rūpa Gosvāmī while Rūpa was laughing at a pastime of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa (the mirror); thinking Rūpa laughed at him, he went away hurt and Rūpa lost the vision; Sanātana explained, and he begged Rūpa's pardon in tears (Bhakti-ratnākara 5.3805-3835).

The old brāhmaṇa whom Jāhnavā-devī and her devotees met at Ekacakrā, the deserted village where he alone had stayed, hoping Nityānanda would return. He told them the history of the place (the Pāṇḍavas and Baka; Ekacakreśvara) and of Nityānanda's birth, childhood and sannyāsa, and wept «O Nitāi!» (Bhakti-ratnākara 11).
